text:
maya: Heads up - alerting for repeated OOMs (OOM: cudaMalloc failed) on gpu-runtime-3 serving openmodel-xlarge. High tail memory growth, spike during long-chat flows. Can we get a mitigation playbook right now?

sam: On it. Quick triage: is traffic concentrated on a single model version? any recent kernel/quant changes rolled?

maya: Yes, 20260221 build bumped the mixed-kernel selector and increased workspace to 1.2x for perf tests. Traffic spike started ~10:45 UTC.

li: Priority temporary mitigations to buy time: 1) flip runtime to the smaller kernel variant for that model 2) enforce per-request token cap + request-shaping 3) reduce workspace size env var 4) force KV cache aggressive eviction.

carla: How do we flip the kernel quickly? is it a route config change?

sam: We can patch the route to prefer kernel=v1-safe. Quick command (internal controlplane):
```
curl -s -X POST https://controlplane.internal/redwood/routes/patch \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"route":"/openmodel-xlarge","patch":{"kernel_preference":"v1-safe"}}'
```
That will route new requests to the safe kernel within ~10s.

andre: Also recommend setting the per-request workspace override to 0.8x at runtime: set REDWOOD_WORKSPACE_MULTIPLIER=0.8 on gpu-runtime-3. That keeps peak memory down while slightly hurting perf.

li: For KV cache: set eviction policy to LRU and drop kvcache.max_items to 30k for this worker pool. Example patch via console API:
```
{
  "pool": "gpu-runtime-3",
  "kvcache": {
    "policy": "lru",
    "max_items": 30000,
    "ttl_seconds": 120
  }
}
```
That should reclaim prefixes quickly.

maya: Can we add a circuit breaker to reject huge inputs instead of OOMing?

sam: Yes. Add a request-shaping policy to the route. Minimal policy to apply immediately:
```
{
  "route": "/openmodel-xlarge",
  "shaper": {
    "max_input_tokens": 2000,
    "max_total_tokens": 4096,
    "concurrency_limit": 12,
    "reject_on_exceed": true
  }
}
```
If clients hit limit they'll get 429 + body explaining to retry with shorter input.

oncall-ops: Applying kernel flip + workspace multiplier + kvcache change now. Will post status.

devops-bot: rollout started: kernel_preference=v1-safe on 3 nodes (gpu-runtime-3). CI guard: none.

carla: I pulled a quick mem profile from 1 of the worker pods before the flip:
```
2026-03-08T10:44:57Z worker-12: GPU mem total=48GB, used=45.3GB; allocator arenas=6; workspace_alloc=5.1GB; kv_cache=8.7GB; unexpected_fragmentation=2.4GB
peak_allocation_sequence: [0.2GB, 1.1GB, 12.8GB, 18.3GB, 45.3GB]
```
Shows steady growth coinciding with long chats.

andre: Fragmentation + workspace bump likely cause. We have two long-term levers: safer allocator tuning (reduce arena count, enable best-fit) and more aggressive buffer reuse. But don't do those mid-incident unless can A/B. For now the traffic-steering + kernel flip is safest.

li: Playbook checklist (short):
1) Flip to safe kernel variant.
2) Decrease REDWOOD_WORKSPACE_MULTIPLIER to 0.8.
3) Apply KV cache LRU + small max_items + ttl.
4) Deploy request shaper (max_input_tokens, concurrency_limit).
5) Monitor for 2x decrease in tail mem and 200s rolling OOM count.
6) If still unstable: failover traffic to openmodel-large (smaller memory footprint) and open incident bridge.

maya: Executed steps 1-4. Observability: tail memory percentile dropped ~18% in 2 minutes, OOM count went from 12/min to 1/min.

sam: Good. Follow-up root-cause actions (post-incident):
- Revert workspace multiplier to testable increment (0.9) in canary and run long-profile.
- Add regression test: synthetic long-chat workload that exercises KV eviction and measures fragmentation every 5k tokens.
- Benchmark kernel selector with AKS of sequences >4k tokens; add fallback to v1-safe earlier in pipeline.
- Consider allocator change: reduce cudaMalloc arenas from 6 -> 3 and enable buffer pooling for small slices.

carla: For the regression test I have a harness ready. I'll run it against the 20260221 build and current canary.

li: Also add a proactive alert: if workspace_alloc > 9GB OR fragmentation > 2GB for 3 consecutive minutes, auto-enable request-shaper for the route and notify #oncall. That prevents future silent spikes.

oncall-ops: done - alert rule added. Thresholds: workspace_alloc > 9GB, kv_cache_items > 45k, fragmentation > 2GB. Timeline: 3m window.

devops-bot: rollout complete: kernel_preference=v1-safe (3/3 nodes), kvcache policy LRU applied, workspace_multiplier set to 0.8.

maya: Incident reduced to "warning". Thanks team.

andre: Postmortem action items: 1) add unit test for kernel selector under mixed sequences, 2) formalize request-shaper template in runtime library, 3) evaluate on-the-fly allocator param toggles.

li: I'm adding a short runbook snippet to the repo for oncall quick steps (copy-paste ready).

Runbook snippet:
```
# OOM mitigation quick steps
1) Controlplane: patch route kernel_preference -> v1-safe
2) Set REDWOOD_WORKSPACE_MULTIPLIER=0.8 on effected pool
3) Patch kvcache: policy=lru, max_items=30000, ttl_seconds=120
4) Apply request-shaper: max_input_tokens=2000, concurrency_limit=12
5) If OOMs persist: fail traffic to smaller model variant
6) Open incident bridge and start postmortem
```

maya: Copy that into #postmortems after this closes. Closing thread once postmortem doc is created. :thumbsup:

sam: Will follow up with perf numbers and a PR for safer default workspace in 2 days.

carla: I'll queue the regression runs now.

oncall-ops: marking incident as mitigated at 2026-03-08T10:55:50Z.
